requirement: Give every issued JWT a unique jti, reject revoked tokens by jti, keep revocation idempotent, and let the list shrink once revoked tokens have expired anyway.
skeleton: RevokedTokenError and a TokenService class with a secret length check, issue adding a uuid jti, a private _decode requiring jti, verify checking the list, revoke storing jti to exp, and purge by exp.
caption: Per-token JWT revocation with PyJWT, HS256 and uuid. RevokedTokenError subclasses jwt.InvalidTokenError. TokenService(secret, ttl) raises ValueError saying the secret must be at least 32 bytes when its UTF-8 encoding is shorter, and keeps an instance dict mapping revoked jti to exp. issue(subject) signs sub, a fresh uuid4 hex jti, iat and exp = now plus ttl. A private _decode pins algorithms to HS256 and requires sub, jti and exp, so a token without jti raises jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError. verify(token) decodes and raises RevokedTokenError naming the jti when it is on the list. revoke(token) uses _decode, not verify, so revoking twice is harmless, and stores the jti with its integer exp. purge(now) forgets every revocation whose exp is at or before now and returns how many it forgot; revoked_count is a property with the list size. The fixture asserts that a revoked token raises RevokedTokenError, that revoking one of two tokens for alice leaves the other valid, that revoking twice leaves a count of 1, that purge at exp minus 1 forgets nothing while purge at exp forgets it, that a token without jti raises jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError, and that a 31 byte secret raises ValueError while 32 bytes is accepted.

plan.intent: Log out individual tokens before they expire
constraints: Every token gets its own random jti
Revoked tokens raise RevokedTokenError while other tokens stay valid
Revoking the same token twice is harmless
Revocations are forgotten once now reaches their exp
A token without jti raises jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError
Secrets shorter than 32 bytes raise ValueError

rationale.teaches: Revoke by a per-token jti, require it at decode time, and bound the list by each token's exp so it never grows forever.
rationale.why: Revoking by subject logs out every device, a shared jti revokes unrelated tokens, and a list that is never purged grows with every logout.

ops.docstring: Revoke individual JWTs by jti and forget each revocation once the token expires.

ops.source:
class RevokedTokenError(jwt.InvalidTokenError):
    """The token's jti is on the revocation list."""

candidates.why_wrong: The jti is generated once per service, so revoking one token revokes every token it issued.
verify never consults the revocation list, so revoked tokens keep working.
A revocation whose exp equals now is kept one tick too long.
jti is not required, so a token without it crashes with KeyError instead of a JWT error.
revoke goes through verify, so revoking an already revoked token raises.
